title: Gemini Robotics 2 adds whole-body control, dexterity and robot teamwork
friendlyTitle: Google’s new AI helps robots move, use their hands and work together
summary: Google DeepMind introduced a three-model Gemini Robotics 2 family for whole-body control, embodied reasoning and local on-device operation. Demonstrations span humanoid movement, two-handed manipulation and teams of robots, although published results show that several multi-finger tasks remain difficult.
friendlySummary: Gemini Robotics 2 can plan tasks and control different kinds of robots, including humanoids. Some versions run on the robot itself, but difficult hand movements still have mixed success.
whyItMatters: The architecture separates high-level planning from physical control and offers a path to adapting one system across different robot bodies. The reasoning model is available in preview, while the control models remain limited to early-access partners, so broad real-world reliability is not yet established.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may help useful robots adapt to more homes and workplaces. Most people cannot use the full system yet, and robots still need testing before they can work safely around people.
